newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin backs economic programme for Russia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin backs economic programme for Russia.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin gave his backing on Monday to a programme of short-term measures drawn up by the cabinet to help kick-start Russia's depressed economy, Interfax news agency said.
"This is not a declaration, not just statistics, but rather a business document which addresses every problem facing each Russian and the country on the whole," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.

"I have a high assessment of this document and put my signature to it," Yeltsin said during a Kremlin meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, first deputy premiers, Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, and Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Sysuyev.

Interfax said the economic plan prepared by the government contained six points but gave no further details. A joint news conference by Chernomyrdin, Nemtsov, Chubais and Sysuyev was scheduled for 3 p.m. (1100 GMT).

Yeltsin, worried about worsening social conditions in Russia and wide public discontent about long delays in wages and pensions, dramatically reshuffled his government earlier this year, putting pro-market liberals in control of the economy.
The government is currently trying to correct its 1997 budget, whose targets are widely seen as too optimistic, and to boost tax revenues to maintain major spending programmes.
